lede: Before he was told to warn anyone, he was told to rise in the dark and recite. “We are about to cast upon you a weighty word” — and the strength to carry it was to be found in the hours when everyone else was asleep.

names.name: al-Muzzammil
names.note: After the way it addresses the Prophet ﷺ in its first ayah: you who are wrapped in your garment.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records agreement that it is Makkan, and then the exceptions that are reported: from Ibn ʿAbbās, that ayat 10 and 11 are Madinan; and from Ibn Yasār and Muqātil, that its last ayah is. That last ayah is unlike the rest of the surah in length and in subject — it speaks of zakāh and of those who will fight in the way of Allah — and ʿĀʾishah relates that it came down twelve months after the opening. The traditional order places the surah third.
revelation.when: The very beginning of the mission; its closing ayah a year or more afterwards

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ المُزَّمِّلِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ، إلّا أنَّهُ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: سِوى آيَتَيْنِ مِنها
مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَجَابِرٍ. وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَقَتَادَةُ: إِلَّا آيَتَيْنِ مِنْهَا

setting: It is among the first three or four surahs to come down. The Prophet ﷺ had seen the angel, had returned to his house shaken, and had asked to be covered. The address reaches him there: O you wrapped up in your cloak — stand.

What he is told to stand for is not, yet, the public call. It is the night: half of it, or a little less, or a little more, reciting the Qurʾan slowly and distinctly. The reason is given in the next breath. We shall soon cast upon you a weighty word. The rising by night makes the deepest impression and the truest speech; by day you have long business to attend to.

ʿĀʾishah tells what followed. Allah made the night prayer obligatory at the opening of this surah, and the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions stood for a year, until their feet swelled. Allah held back its ending in the heaven for twelve months; then He sent down the lightening in its final ayah, and standing by night became voluntary after it had been required.
So the first generation of Muslims was formed, before anything else was asked of them, by a year of nights.

occasions.title: The lightening
occasions.text: “Allah made standing by night obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions stood for a year. Allah withheld its conclusion for twelve months in the heaven, until He sent down the lightening at the end of this surah, and standing by night became voluntary after having been obligatory.”

aim: To set out the spiritual provision of those who call to Allah, in the face of hardship and the difficulties of life — steadying the Prophet ﷺ, and threatening those who deny him.

outline.title: Rise by night
outline.summary: O you wrapped up: stand through the night, all but a little — half of it, or a little less, or more — and recite the Qurʾan in slow, measured tones. We shall cast upon you a weighty word. The hours of the night are firmer of tread and truer of speech. Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him wholly: Lord of the east and the west, there is no god but He, so take Him as your trustee.

outline.title: Bear with them
outline.summary: Be patient with what they say, and part from them in a gracious manner. Leave Me to deal with the deniers, those who live in ease, and give them a little time: with Us are shackles and a blaze, food that chokes and a painful punishment, on the Day the earth and the mountains shake.

outline.title: A messenger, as to Pharaoh
outline.summary: We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh. Pharaoh disobeyed, and We seized him with a crushing grip. How then will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn children grey? This is a reminder: let whoever wills take a way to his Lord.

outline.title: The lightening
outline.summary: Your Lord knows that you stand nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third, and a group of those with you. He knows you cannot keep count of it, and has turned to you in mercy: so recite what is easy of the Qurʾan. He knows that there will be among you the sick, and others travelling the land in search of Allah’s bounty, and others fighting in His cause. So recite what is easy of it, establish the prayer, give the zakāh, and lend Allah a goodly loan.

keyAyah.why: How the Qurʾan is to be recited, in the Qurʾan’s own words: tartīl — slowly, distinctly, with thought.

virtues.text: Saʿd ibn Hishām asked ʿĀʾishah about the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: “Do you not read ‘O you wrapped up’? Allah made standing by night obligatory at the beginning of this surah…”

before: Al-Jinn ended with the Messenger ﷺ commanded to convey what his Lord sent. Al-Muzzammil shows how he was prepared to carry it.
after: Al-Muzzammil: stand, by night, before your Lord. Al-Muddaththir: stand, and warn the people. The two openings are a pair — the private preparation and the public task.
